en: The expression μαϑητεύσατε βαπτίζοντες is therefore of deep significance. — “All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (so Jesus speaks in John

13, 31 of his glorification, at the moment when Judas had left the company in order to betray Jesus to the Jews, — at the point in time when he looked forward to the home-coming to his Father, who is greater than he; here, where he is presented as already taken out of everything that the world could demand of him, could have a part in him), — “All power has been given to me, in heaven and on earth; therefore go forth to all peoples, and your making of disciples shall be that you initiate them into the relation of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, so that it [they] may flow around and encompass them as the water does the one dipped in water, in all points of their being — and behold, I am with you through the whole of the days until the consummation of the world.”
At this point in time, where Jesus is presented as raised above all actuality and personality, there can least of all be thought an individuality, a personality of his being.
He is with them, whose being is permeated by the divine Spirit, who are initiated into the divine, whose being is alive in the divine that is now consummated in him.
zh: 所以“μαϑητεύσατε βαπτίζοντες”这个说法含义很深。——“天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了”（耶稣在《约翰福音》

13, 31 谈他的得荣耀，那是在犹大离开这一伙人、要把耶稣出卖给犹太人的那一刻，——在他盼望着回到那位比他更大的父那里去的那个时刻；在这里，他被设想为已经从世界可能向他要求的一切、从世界可能分有他的一切中抽身出来了），——“天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了；所以你们要去，使万民作门徒，而你们使人作门徒，就是把他们引入父、子和神圣的精神的关系之中，让这关系像水环抱那浸入水中的人一样，在他们本质的一切点上环绕他们、把他们整个包住——看哪，我同你们在一起，度过全部的日子，直到世界的终了。”
在这个时刻，耶稣被表现为超脱了一切现实性和位格，最不可能去设想他的本质还有什么个体性、什么位格。
他与他们同在：他们的本质被神性的精神渗透，他们被引入神性之中，他们的本质就在那如今在他身上完成了的神性里活着。

en: The immersion into the relation of the Father, the Son and the Spirit Luke expresses much more weakly (Luke

24, 47) than as a proclamation in the name of the Christ, — of the change of mind and the release of sins; a proclamation that should begin in Jerusalem; they were witnesses of what had happened, he would send them the promise of his Father, and they should not begin their work outside Jerusalem until they were clothed with the power from on high. — A mere doctrine can be proclaimed and supported by the testimony of things that have happened, without its own holy Spirit; but such a teaching would be no consecration, no immersion of the Spirit.

In Mark — if the last chapter were not entirely genuine, its tone is nonetheless characteristic — this farewell of Jesus is expressed much more objectively; the spiritual appears in it more as an ordinary formula, the expressions [are] customary words grown cold through the habit of a church: Proclaim the gospel (without further addition, a kind of terminus technicus), the believer and the baptized will be saved, the unbeliever will be condemned, — the believer and the baptized already have the look of definite soulless words serving a sect or congregation as a badge, whose full concepts are presupposed.

Instead of the spirited [word]: I am with you all days, the being-filled of the believers with the Spirit of God and of the glorified Jesus, Mark speaks drily, without its being lifted by inspiration and breathing with spirit, of wonderful masteries of actuality, of casting out devils and similar actions that the believers will be capable of, as objectively as one can speak of actions without mentioning their soul.
zh: 浸入父、子和精神的关系这一点，路加表达得弱得多（《路加福音》
24, 47），他只把它说成奉基督之名的宣讲——宣讲悔改和罪的赦免；这宣讲应当从耶路撒冷开始；他们是所发生之事的见证人，他要把父的应许赐给他们，而他们在耶路撒冷之外不可先开始自己的工作，直到他们穿上从上头来的能力。——单纯的学说可以宣讲，也可以靠已发生之事的见证来支撑，并不需要自己特有的神圣的精神；但这样的教导就不是圣化，不是精神的浸入。

在《马可福音》里——即使最后一章不完全是真的，它的语气也还是有代表性的——耶稣的这次告别表达得客观得多；精神性的东西在他那里更像是普通的套语，那些说法是靠一个教会的习惯冷下来的常用词：传福音（不加进一步的补充，一种 terminus technicus），信的和受洗的必得救，不信的必被定罪，——信的和受洗的人已经带上了某些没有灵魂的用词的样子，这些词充当教派或教团的标记，而它们的完整概念是被预设了的。
马可不说那句有精神的话——我天天与你们同在，不说信徒被上帝的精神和得荣耀的耶稣所充满，而是干巴巴地讲，没有因热忱而提升、也没有精神吹拂，讲对现实性的奇妙支配，讲赶鬼和诸如此类信徒将来能够做到的行为，讲得尽可能客观，却丝毫不提这些行为的灵魂。

en: The development of the divine in human beings, the relation into which they enter with God through being filled with the holy Spirit, to become his sons and to live in the harmony of their whole being and character, of their developed manifoldness, a harmony in which not [only] their many-sided consciousness rings together into one spirit, the many shapes of life into one life, but through which also the dividing walls against other godlike beings are sublated and the same living Spirit animates the different beings, which are therefore no longer merely alike but at one, do not form an assembly but a congregation, because they are united not in a universal, a concept, say as believers, but through life, through love, — this living harmony of human beings, their community in God, Jesus calls the kingdom of God. — The Jewish language gave him the word kingdom, which brings something heterogeneous into the expression of the divine union of human beings, since it signifies only a unity through ruling, through the violence of one stranger over another stranger, which must be entirely removed from the beauty and the divine life of a pure league of human beings — the freest thing that is possible.

This idea of a kingdom of God completes and comprises the whole of the religion as Jesus founded it, and it is still to be considered whether it satisfies nature completely, or what need drove his disciples to something further.

In the kingdom of God the common element is that all are alive in God, not the common element in a concept, but love, a living bond that unites the believers, this feeling of the oneness of life, in which all oppositions, as such enmities, and also the unions of the existing oppositions, — rights are sublated; a new commandment I give you, says Jesus, that you love one another, by this shall one recognize that you are my disciples.
This friendship of souls, expressed as essence, as spirit for reflection, is the divine Spirit, God, who rules the congregation.

Is there a more beautiful idea than a people of human beings related to one another through love? a more elevating one than to belong to a whole that, as a whole, as one, is the Spirit of God, — whose sons the individuals are?
Should there still be an incompleteness in this idea, that a fate had power in it? or would this fate be the Nemesis that raged against too beautiful a striving, against an overleaping of nature?
zh: 神圣者在人里面的发展，人因被神圣的精神充满而与上帝进入的那种关系——成为他的儿子，并且在他们整个本质和性格、在他们已发展出来的杂多的和谐中生活，这样一种和谐：在其中，不只是他们多方面的意识汇成一个精神、众多生命形态汇成一个生命，而且通过它，与别的类似神的存在者之间的隔墙也被扬弃，同一个活生生的精神赋予这些不同的存在者以灵魂，于是他们不再只是相同，而是合而为一，不是凑成一个聚集，而是一个教团，因为他们不是在一个普遍者、一个概念里——比如说作为信徒——结合起来，而是通过生命、通过爱结合起来的，——人这种活生生的和谐，他们在上帝中的共同体，耶稣称之为上帝之国。——犹太人的语言给了他“王国”这个词，这个词把某种异质的东西带进了对人的神圣结合的表述，因为它所表示的只是一种通过统治、通过一个陌生者对另一个陌生者的暴力而来的统一，这种统一必须完全从纯粹人类联合体的美和神圣生命中排除出去——那是可能的东西中最自由的东西。
上帝之国这个理念，把耶稣所创立的那种宗教整体加以完成，并且把它包含在内，而还有待考察的是：它是否完全满足了本性，或者说，是哪种需要把他的门徒逼向了更远的东西。
在上帝之国里，共同的东西在于一切人都活在上帝之中，不是在一个概念里的共同，而是爱，是一条活生生的纽带，把信徒们联合起来，是这种对生命之一体的感受：在其中，一切对立，作为对立也就是敌意，连同现存对立之间的种种结合，——连同权利，都被扬弃了；我赐给你们一条新诫命，耶稣说，就是你们要彼此相爱，人们由此就应当认出你们是我的门徒。
这种灵魂的友谊，作为本质、作为为反思而说出的精神，就是神性的精神，就是统治着教团的上帝。
还有比一群通过爱相互关联的人更美的理念吗？还有比属于一个整体更令人提升的吗——这个整体作为整体、作为一，就是上帝的精神，而各个个人则是它的儿子？
这个理念里是否还留有一种不完整，即命运在其中还有力量？或者这命运就是那位复仇女神，她向过于美好的追求、向对自然的逾越发怒？

en: In love the human being has found himself again in another; because it is a union of life, it presupposed separation, a development, a cultivated many-sidedness of the same; and the more shapes life is alive in, the more points it can unite and feel itself in, the more inward love can be; the more extended in manifoldness the relations and feelings of the lovers are, the more inwardly love concentrates itself, the more exclusive it is, the more indifferent to other forms of life; its joy mingles with every other life, acknowledges it, but withdraws at the feeling of an individuality, and the more isolated human beings stand in regard to their cultivation and their interest, [in] their relation to the world, the more peculiar each one has, the more confined love becomes to itself; and in order to have the consciousness of its happiness, in order to give itself that happiness, as it gladly does, it is necessary that it separate itself off, that it even create enmities for itself.

A love among many therefore admits only a certain degree of strength, of inwardness, and demands equality of spirit, of interest, of many conditions of life, a diminution of the individualities; but this commonness of life, this equality of spirit, since it is not love, can come to consciousness only through its definite, strongly marked utterances; of an agreement in knowledge, in the same opinions, there can be no question; the bond of many rests on the same need, it presents itself in objects that can be common, in relations that arise over them, and then in the common striving for the same and in common activity and action; it can attach itself to a thousand objects of common possession and enjoyment and of the same cultivation, and recognize itself in them.

A multitude of the same purposes, the whole extent of physical need, can be the object of united activity; in this the same spirit [presents itself], and this common spirit then also takes pleasure in manifesting itself in rest, in being glad of its union, in enjoying itself in joy and in play.

The friends of Jesus kept together after his death, ate and drank in common, some of their brotherhoods abolished all property right among one another, others partly, in abundant alms and contributions to the congregation; they spoke together of their departed friend and master, prayed in common and strengthened one another in faith and courage; their enemies accused some of their societies also of the community of wives; an accusation that they either did not have the courage and the purity to deserve, or were not ashamed of.
In common many went out to make other peoples partakers of their faith and their hopes; and because this is the only doing of the Christian congregation, proselytism is essentially proper to it.

Beyond this common enjoying, praying, eating, rejoicing, believing and hoping, beyond the single activity for the spread of the faith, the enlargement of the commonness of devotion, there still lies an enormous field of objectivity, which a fate of the most many-sided extent and tremendous power sets up and which calls for manifold activity.
In the task of love the congregation disdains every union that would not be the most inward, every spirit that would not be the highest.

Not to mention the unnaturalness and insipidity of the splendid idea of a universal love of mankind, since it is not the striving of the congregation, the latter must stop at love itself; apart from the relation of the common faith and the presentations of this community in religious actions referring to it, every other connection in something objective, to a purpose, [to] a development of another side of life, to a common activity, every spirit cooperating toward something other than the spread of the faith and presenting itself in other modifications and partial shapes of life, in plays, and rejoicing in itself, is foreign to the congregation, it would not recognize itself in it, it would have let go of love, its only spirit, would have become unfaithful to its God; nor would it merely have left love, it would also have destroyed it; for the members run the danger of colliding with one another in their individualities, and would have to do so all the more since their cultivation was [different] and they would thereby enter the domain of their different characters, the power of their different fates, and over an interest in something slight, over a different determination in something small, love would turn into hatred and a falling away from God would follow.
This danger is averted only by an inactive, undeveloped love, in that it, the highest life, remains unliving.
Thus the unnatural extension of the scope of love entangles it in a contradiction, in a false striving that had to become the father of the most terrible suffering or active fanaticism.

This limitation of love to itself, its flight from all forms, even if its spirit already breathed in them or they sprang from it, this removal from all fate is precisely its greatest fate, and here is the point where Jesus is connected with fate, and indeed in the most sublime way, but suffered from it.
zh: 在爱里，人已经在另一个人身上重新找到了自己；因为爱是生命的一种结合，它就预设了分离，预设了生命的一种发展、一种教养出来的多方面性；生命活在越多的形态里，它能在越多的点上结合自己、感受自己，爱也就越内在；相爱者的关系和感受在杂多上越广，爱越内在、越集中，它就越排他，对其他生命形态就越无所谓；爱的欢乐与每一种别的生命相混，承认它，但一碰到个体性的感受就退回来；而人在教养和利益上、在与世界的关系上越孤立，每个人自己独有的东西越多，爱就越局限于自身；而要意识到自己的幸福，要像它乐意做的那样把幸福给自己，它就必须把自己隔离开来，甚至给自己造出敌意。

因此，许多人之间的爱只容许一定程度的强度、一定程度的亲密，它要求精神、利益、许多生活关系上的一致，要求个体性的减少；但这种生命的共同性、这种精神上的一致，既然不是爱，就只能通过它那些确定而刻画鲜明的表现进入意识；至于认识上的一致、意见相同，那是根本谈不上的；许多人的联结建立在相同的困厄上，它表现在能够共同享有的对象上，表现在由此产生的关系上，然后表现在对这些对象的共同追求以及共同的活动和行动上；它可以附着于成千上万共同占有、共同享受和同等教养的对象，并在其中认出自己。
许多相同的目的、物理需要的整个范围，都可以成为联合起来的活动的对象；在这种活动中呈现出相同的精神，而这种共同的精神也乐于在安宁中表明自己，乐于为自己的结合而高兴，在欢乐和游戏里享受自己。
耶稣的朋友在他死后聚在一起，共同吃喝，他们的一些兄弟会彼此之间取消了全部财产权，另一些则部分取消，办法是丰厚的施舍和向教团缴纳的献款；他们一起谈论他们已离去的朋友和老师，共同祈祷，在信仰和勇气上互相坚固；他们的敌人也指责他们的一些团体共妻；这项指责，他们要么没有勇气和纯洁去配得上，要么并不为它感到羞耻。
许多人一同出去，要让别的民族分有他们的信仰和他们的希望；而因为这是基督教教团唯一的作为，所以劝人入教对教团来说是本质上固有的。
除了这种共同的享受、祈祷、吃喝、欢乐、信仰和希望，除了为传播信仰、扩大虔诚之共同性这一唯一的作为，还横着一片巨大的客观性领域，它是由一种范围和力量都极其广大、极其强横的命运摆出来的，并且要求人多方面地行动。
在爱所提出的任务里，教团鄙视一切不是最内在的结合，鄙视一切不是最高的精神。

不必提普遍人类之爱那个漂亮理念的不自然和乏味了，因为它并不是教团的追求，教团必然停在爱本身那里；除了共同信仰的关系以及这种共同体在与之相关的宗教行为中的种种表现，任何别的联系——联系在某种客观的东西上、联系在一个目的上、联系在生命另一个方面的发展上、联系在共同的活动上，任何向着传播信仰以外的东西共同起作用、并在生命的其他变体和局部形态中、在游戏里表现出来并为之欣喜的精神——对教团来说都是陌生的，教团在它里面不会认出自己，它就等于离开了爱、离开了它唯一的精神，等于对自己的上帝不忠；而且它不只是离开了爱，还会毁掉爱；因为成员们有以各自的个体性互相碰撞的危险，而且必然更加如此，因为他们的教养[各不相同]，他们因此就进入了自己不同性格的领域、自己不同命运的力量之中，于是为了一点点小事的兴趣、为了某个小东西上的不同规定，爱就会变成恨，就会出现对上帝的背离。
这种危险只有靠一种不活动、未发展的爱来避免，也就是让那最高的生命始终没有活气。
爱违反自然地扩大自己的范围，就这样缠进一种矛盾、一种错误的追求，而这种追求必然会成为最可怕的、忍受着的或行动着的狂热的父亲。
爱对自身的这种限制，它对一切形式的逃避——即使它的精神早已在这些形式里吹拂，或者这些形式原本就是从它那里生出来的——这种对一切命运的远离，恰恰就是它最大的命运；而这里就是耶稣与命运相联结的那个点，并且是以最崇高的方式相联结，但他却因命运而受苦。
